_comment: The boundary list. Everything not named here is external, which is the safe
direction to be wrong in: a held message costs one tap, a sent one can't be
recalled.
internal_domains — your own tenancies. Subdomains count. Add a domain here
only if every mailbox on it is yours; a shared or client-run domain is not
internal even if you have an address on it.
external_overrides — addresses on an internal domain that are really outside
parties (shared mailboxes an agency or auditor reads, forwarding aliases).
internal_handles — Slack IDs/channels and phone numbers, which have no domain
to check. Only what's listed here is internal.
sensitive_terms — held even when every recipient is internal. Fundraise,
valuation and personnel matters aren't recoverable once they're in the wrong
internal channel either.
hold_if_contains_figure — the Chief of Staff's own suggestion (1 Aug): a nudge
or status update to the team is safe, but an internal message with a number
in it commits you to that number. Quantified messages are held.
first_time_channels — also its suggestion: it has a 'preview ritual' before
posting to a business channel for the first time, and cites a real incident
behind it. Add a channel here once you've seen it post there cleanly; until
then a first post is held even though the channel is internal.
